Der Einfachheit halber hat der Charakter zu jeder Zeit Zugriff auf den gesamten Inhalt seiner Börse, solange die Börse beim Charakter ist.
Tipp: Die Börse stehlen Charaktere können von anderen Charakteren die Börse stehlen. Es ist stets empfohlen, den Spielercharakteren Optionen zu geben, die gestohlene Börse zurück zu bekommen, um die Frustration beim Schauspieler so gering wie möglich zu halten. Allerdings kann eine gestohlene Börse auch als Handlungspunkt genutzt werden, um die Schauspieler in eine bestimmte Richtung zu bewegen.
Die Behälter "groß" und "klein" sind funktional identisch. Sie beschreiben Mittel, durch die ein Charakter mehr Gegenstände mit sich führen kann, obwohl sein Ausrüstungslimit erreicht ist, oder wenn der Charakter diese Gegenstände bewusst nicht als Ausrüstung führt. Anders als Ausrüstung nehmen hier alle mitgeführten Gegenstände ein Volumen ein, welches durch die Mehrfachmarkierung von entsprechend vielen Inventarplätzen verdeutlicht wird. Gegenstände im Inventar sind für den Charakter nicht direkt zugänglich und müssen erst aus dem Behälter genommen werden, bevor der Charakter diese Gegenstände nutzen kann. Der Hauptunterschied zwischen den beiden Behältern liegt darin, wie viel Platz der Behälter maximal zur Verfügung stellen kann. Der große Behälter bietet deutlich mehr Platz als der kleine Behälter, allerdings ist er etwas schwieriger zu transportieren. Gleichzeitig kann der Erwerb eines großen Behälters ein höheres Investment für den Charakter bedeuten.
Beispiel: Im Gefecht auf Behälter zugreifen Gabe der Minenarbeiter trägt seine wertvolle Spitzhacke stets geholstert an seinem Rücken, anstelle sie zu verstauen, was dem Schauspieler erlaubt, sie als Ausrüstung zu markieren. Jetzt wurde er im Tunnel von einem Goblin konfrontiert.
Dieser weiß nicht so recht, was er genau tun will, und so ist Gabe direkt am Zug. Er zückt seine Spitzhacke und nutzt gleichzeitig den Schwung der Bewegung, um dem Gegner eine Stichwunde zu verpassen. Das kann Gabe innerhalb einer Aktion durchführen. In der nächsten Runde will er seine Taschenlampe zücken, um den Goblin zu blenden und sich so einen Vorteil zu verschaffen, doch diese Taschenlampe ist nicht wie sonst an seinem Gürtel befestigt, sondern in einer Tasche seines Blaumanns verstaut. Auf mechanischer Ebene ist die Lampe nur in Gabes kleinem Behälter, nicht aber in seiner Ausrüstung.
Gabe muss also eine Aktion verwenden, um die Taschenlampe aus der Tasche zu holen, erst dann kann er in der nächsten Runde den Gegner mit einem gezielten Leuchtkegel blenden.
Verschieden große Gegenstände verbrauchen unterschiedlich viel Platz. Dieser Platzverbrauch ist ausschlaggebend dafür, wie viel der Charakter tragen kann.
Wenn ein Charakter einen Gegenstand aufnimmt, schreibt der Schauspieler den Bezeichner des Gegenstandes in den Inventarplatz, den er dafür verwendet. Sollte der Gegenstand mehr als einen Inventarplatz einnehmen, werden entsprechend viele weitere freie Inventarplätze weggestrichen, und beim Entledigen des Gegenstandes wieder geleert.
Beispiel: Gegenstände verstauen Barry der Barde hat seine Laute gerne bei sich. Dieses Instrument ist groß und benötigt somit 3 Inventarplätze. Barrys Schauspieler notiert die Laute im Inventar, und markiert 2 weitere Inventarplätze als belegt.

item.title: Behälter
item.description:
Das Inventar eines Charakters besteht aus drei getrennten Bereichen. Neben der Ausrüstung des Charakters, welche die direkt verfügbaren Gegenstände auflistet, gibt es noch zwei erweiternde Inventare, genannt Behälter, welche die gesamte Tragefähigkeit des Charakters um ein Vielfaches verbessern.
Jeder Charakter hat die Möglichkeit, einen kleinen und einen großen Behälter zu erhalten. Diese nehmen keinen Ausrüstungsplatz ein, sondern werden bei Erhalt auf Seite 4 des Charakterbogens markiert, wodurch die darunter gelisteten Inventarplätze dem Charakter direkt zur Verfügung stehen.Anders als bei Ausrüstung nehmen schwerere oder größere Gegenstände mehr Inventarplätze ein, meist jedoch maximal 3.
Der einzige Unterschied zwischen den beiden Behältern ist die Platzmenge. Der große Behälter fasst doppelt so viel Inventar wie der kleine Behälter. Die Regie ist dazu angehalten, den kleinen Behälter in der Regel leichter zu gewähren als den Großen.Anders als die Ausrüstung jedoch sind die Inhalte der Behälter nicht direkt den Charakteren verfügbar, sondern müssen in zeitkritischen Situationen erst herausgenommen werden.

item.title: Adrenalin
item.description:
Im Laufe einer Geschichte sammeln die Spielercharaktere eine besondere Ressource namens "Adrenalin". Diese Ressource kann genutzt werden, um die Narrative des Spiels in kleinen, aber signifikanten Änderungen zu beeinflussen.
Jeder Spielercharakter hat einen Adrenalinspiegel. Dieser Spiegel steht immer zwischen 0 und einer Obergrenze, welche durch die Stufe des Charakters festgelegt ist.
Zu Beginn einer Geschichte, sowie nach jeder Pause von mindestens 2 Segmenten Stufe 1, setzt sich der Adrenalinspiegel jedes Spielercharakters auf 1 zurück - die Ausnahme bilden Charaktere auf Stufe 0, sie starten immer mit 0 Adrenalin.
Adrenalin kann innerhalb der Geschichte angehäuft werden. Jeder Spielercharakter hat eine oder zwei Adrenalinquellen, welche der Schauspieler des Charakters in Abstimmung mit der Regie bestimmt.
Beispiel: Quelle bestimmen 1 Cliyo ist eine Söldnerin. Ihr Schauspieler wünscht, dass ihre Quelle darin besteht, an der Front zu kämpfen. Die Regie schlägt vor, dass Cliyo immer dann Adrenalin erzeugt, wenn sie mindestens eine Wunde an einem Gegner verursacht. Beispiel: Quelle bestimmen 2 Jason der Förster liebt Rätsel, dies ist eine kleine Eigenheit seines Charakters. Er hat ein hohes Wits-Attribut, und sein Hobby ist es, regelmäßig Rätsel zu lösen. Jasons Schauspieler und die Regie einigen sich, dass Jason immer dann Adrenalin erzeugt, wenn Jason eine untypische aber mögliche Lösung für ein vorliegendes Problem finden kann.
Um angesammeltes Adrenalin zu nutzen, bewirkt der Charakter einen Adrenalinrausch. Hierfür wählt der Schauspieler einen Effekt aus dieser Liste aus, und bezahlt die Menge an Adrenalin, um den Effekt zu nutzen:
Mehr Glück als Verstand - oder Kraft, oder Eleganz, oder Charme (1 Adrenalin, einmalig pro Probe): Die aktuelle nicht gemischte Probe kann mit Luck gemischt werden. Für bereits gemischte Proben kann diese Option nicht genutzt werden.
Reines Glück (1 Adrenalin, so oft wie gewünscht): Der Ausgang der aktuellen Probe wird um eine Stufe verbessert.
Das Drehbuch drehen (2 Adrenalin, einmalig pro Szene): Der Schauspieler darf rückwirkend die Szene durch eine kleine Änderung zugunsten des Charakters abändern. Die Regie muss der Änderung zustimmen, andernfalls muss der Schauspieler etwas anderes wählen.
Beispiel: Adrenalinrausch Die Söldnerin Cliyo hat ihr Maximum von 3 Adrenalin erreicht. Als sie eine Höhle betritt, ohne sich vorher vorzubereiten, kündigt ihr Schauspieler an, mithilfe von 2 Adrenalin das Drehbuch zu drehen und am Eingang der Höhle eine Öllampe zu platzieren. Die Regie stimmt zu, unter der Bedingung, dass die Lampe fast leer ist, und Cliyo mit dem Licht sparsam umgehen muss. Das übrige Adrenalin verbleibt auf dem Charakterbogen, und Cliyo kann später einen weiteren Adrenalinrausch nutzen.

item.title: Gormott
item.description: Ein riesiger, giraffenartiger Titan, dessen Rücken von üppigen Wäldern und weiten Grasebenen bedeckt ist. Einst eine unabhängige Republik der Gormotti, heute unter der Besatzung des Kaiserreichs Mor Ardain als "Gormott-Provinz" verwaltet.Der Titan Gormott ist von dichten Wäldern, offenen Ebenen und Klippen geprägt. Zugängliche Bereiche verändern sich mit den Bewegungen des Wolkenmeers, in das der Titan eingebettet ist. Die Hauptsiedlung der Gormotti ist Torigoth, nahe derer die Ruinen des Weißen Stuhls liegen — der einstige Regierungssitz der unabhängigen Republik Gormott, zerstört im Zuge der ardainischen Eroberung vor rund 50 Jahren (siehe Fraktionen/Republik Gormott.md). Die Trümmer sind politisch bis heute aufgeladen: ein sichtbares Symbol der verlorenen Souveränität, direkt vor den Toren der Besatzungsverwaltung.Die Gormotti (eigene Abstammung, siehe Abstammungen/Gormotti.md): menschenähnliche, aber biologisch eigenständige Bewohner mit katzenartigen Merkmalen, insbesondere beweglichen Ohren, feinem Fell und krallenartigen Fingernägeln. Sie lebten bis vor relativ kurzer Zeit als unabhängige Republik, bevor Mor Ardain den Titan im Zuge einer Ressourcenkrise militärisch eroberte und seither als Provinz besetzt hält. Kaiserreich Mor Ardain (Besatzungsmacht, unterhält u.a. die Torigoth-Relaisbasis) — eigene Datei unter Fraktionen/Mor Ardain.md. Republik Gormott (Reste der ehemals unabhängigen gormottischen Selbstverwaltung, inzwischen der Besatzung untergeordnet) — eigene Datei unter Fraktionen/Republik Gormott.md. Gormott wird seit knapp 50 Jahren von Mor Ardain belagert. Eine eigene Armee gab es zu Zeiten des Weißen Stuhls, jedoch wurde die Armee durch das Imperium aufgelöst. Stattdessen steht jedem Stamm in Gormott eine kleine Gruppe Kämpfern zur Verfügung. Einige Gormotti sehen dies nicht als Unterdrückung an, sondern als Schutz, da das Imperium mit der Gormotti Kultur nicht interferiert.Gleichzeitig ist Gormott Zankapfel zwischen Mor Ardain und dem Königreich Uraya, das die Annexion als Angriff auf den eigenen Einflussbereich wertet — die Provinz liegt damit im Zentrum eines drohenden größeren Konflikts zwischen beiden Großmächten. Ein Auftrag, der die Spieler zwischen die Fronten von Besatzern und einheimischem Widerstand stellt. Uraya sucht heimlich Verbündete unter den Gormotti, um Mor Ardain zu schwächen — die Spieler könnten als Mittelsmänner fungieren oder genau das verhindern sollen.

item.title: KeyCard
item.description: Zugangskarte für Mitarbeiter des FBC, welche die Bewegungsbefugnisse der Mitarbeiter regeln BeDieser Gegenstand muss in ein entsprechendes Kartenlesegerät gesteckt werden, um zu wirken. Qualität hängt vom Rang des Mitarbeiters ab, kann nicht ohne weiteres verändert werden 1 - Intern 2 - Security 3 - Teamleitung 4 - Abteilungsleitung 5 - Geschäftsführung hierarchisch

item.title: Clearance
item.description:
Bildet ab, wie Zugangsrechte im Ältesten Haus über abgestufte Clearance-Level und dazu passende KeyCards geregelt werden.
Abgeriegelte Bereiche verlangen ein Clearance-Level, welches über die KeyCard der Mitarbeiter nachgewiesen wird Clearance ist Minimumwert, festgehalten als Qualität auf der KeyCard als Ausrüstung Clearance-Level hängt vom Rang der Mitarbeiter ab An bestimmten Stationen kann ein Charakter mit höherer Clearance einem Charakter mit geringerer Clearance diese anheben dazu sind die KeyCards von beiden Charakteren in die Station zu geben Die Clearance des zweiten Charakters wird mit der Clearance des ersten Charakters überschrieben
Clearance ist dargestellt als numerischer Wert, der auf der KeyCard der Mitarbeiter gespeichert wurde Die Clearance-Level sind: 1 - Intern 2 - Security 3 - Teamleitung 4 - Abteilungsleitung 5 - Geschäftsführung Jeder Mitarbeiter bekommt eine KeyCard mit einem passenden Clearance-Level von 1 bis 4, je nach Rang
Der Clearance-Level von Mitarbeitern in Central Executive ist 1 Level höher als

item.title: Altered World Events
item.description:
Beschreibt den Mechanismus, über den ein gewöhnlicher Gegenstand oder Ort zu einem Altered Item bzw. Object of Power wird. Ausgelöst durch das kollektive Unbewusste: teilen viele Menschen unbewusst dasselbe archetypische Bild/dieselbe Bedeutung über einen Gegenstand/Ort, kann dieser „kippen" und Anomalien annehmen Historischer Begriff vor 1964: „Paradimensional Occurrence", danach „Altered World Event" (AWE) Beispiel „The Oscillator": ein Ventilator, im echten Leben nur Grundlage eines koreanischen Aberglaubens („Fan Death") — im Bureau-Kanon entzieht der Ventilator tatsächlich Sauerstoff und tötet, während das Bureau selbst den „nur Aberglaube"-Mythos als Vertuschung in die echte Welt gestreut hat Traumatische/unheimliche Umstände (Todesfälle, Verschwinden, obsessive Aufmerksamkeit) wirken oft als Auslöser, wo keine fertige Sagen-Vorlage existiert Ein AWE kann auch durch Kontakt mit einem bereits bestehenden Object of Power ausgelöst werden, statt spontan zu entstehen Setting-Nebenregel: nur ausreichend „archetypische"/altehrwürdige Technik funktioniert in paranormal durchdrungenen Bereichen des Hauses (Radios, Projektoren, Disketten) — modernere Digitaltechnik (Smartphones, Laptops) gilt als „zu neu" für das kollektive Unbewusste und versagt dort Spontane AWEs — kollektives Unbewusstes verändert ein Objekt/einen Ort über Zeit Ausgelöste AWEs — Kontakt mit einem bestehenden Object of Power reißt eine neue Verbindung auf Untersuchungssektor überwacht laufende/bekannte AWE-Fälle
Research führt die wissenschaftliche Auswertung durch

item.title: Astralreisen & Thresholds
item.description:
Beschreibt, wie Charaktere zwischen dem Ältesten Haus, der Astralebene und anderen Dimensionen reisen — über Thresholds, den Diaprojektor und ähnliche Objects of Power. Thresholds sind spontan auftretende Verbindungen zwischen dem Ältesten Haus und anderen Dimensionen Der Diaprojektor öffnet gezielt Portale zu anderen Dimensionen über Dias Berührung eines Objects of Power kann unfreiwillig in die Astralebene teleportieren Rückkehr aus der Astralebene läuft oft über einfache Trigger (z.B. eine schimmernde Kugel auf einem Podest) statt eigener Steuerung
Diaprojektor — laut Bureau-Unterlagen nie von einem Parautilitarier gebunden worden, aktiviert sich auch ungebunden von selbst
Dimensionale Brücke — Rekonstruktion des Portalzugangs, aktuell von Jesse Faden und Emily Pope genutzt
Quarry Threshold im Wartungssektor — Verbindung zu einer weiteren Dimension, in der Black Rock abgebaut wird
Reguliert durch Research und Central Executive Seit der Zischen-Invasion strengere Vorsichtsmaßnahmen, insbesondere bei Dimensionaler Forschung und Blackrock Quarry

item.title: Objects of Power & Altered Items
item.description:
Beschreibt die Unterscheidung zwischen gewöhnlichen Veränderten Gegenständen (Altered Items) und den selteneren, mächtigeren Objects of Power. Objects of Power sind mit der Astralebene und dem Vorstand verbunden — Berührung teleportiert unfreiwillig in die Astralebene Ein Parautilitarier kann sich per Ritual dauerhaft an ein Object of Power binden und erhält dessen Fähigkeit Altered Items haben diese Astralebenen-Verbindung nicht und können nicht gebunden werden, wirken aber dennoch anomal auf ihre Umgebung Die Grenze zwischen beiden Kategorien gilt laut Bureau selbst als „durchaus unklar" — manche Objekte sind in beiden Katalogen gleichzeitig gelistet (z.B. Arctic Queen/Kühlschrank, Ocelot's Anchor) Mechanisch nutzen beide Kategorien dasselbe Gegenstand-Schema (Qualität 1–5 + Tags), keine eigene Tier-Achse Katalogisierung über Kürzel AI##/OOP## + zwei Buchstaben (KE, PE, UE, AE, BE) — Bedeutung der Buchstaben ist selbst dem Bureau nicht bekannt, bewusst offen gelassenes Mysterium Objects of Power — siehe einzelne Gegenstandsdateien unter Gegenstände/ Altered Items — siehe einzelne Gegenstandsdateien unter Gegenstände/ Für die meisten laut Bureau-Katalog dokumentierten Objekte (über 100 OoP, über 40 Altered Items) existiert vorerst nur eine leere Vorlage — erst bei tatsächlicher Erwähnung im Spiel ausbauen
Wie ein gewöhnlicher Gegenstand überhaupt erst zu einem Altered Item oder Object of Power wird: siehe Altered World Events
Containment verwaltet und katalogisiert beide Kategorien
Research darf zu Forschungszwecken darauf zugreifen

item.title: Fadens Säuberung des Hauses
item.description:
Jesse Faden bindet die Amtswaffe und wird vom Vorstand als neue Direktorin bestätigt Vertreibt das Zischen mithilfe des Diaprojektors aus dem Großteil des Hauses - Nach Der Zischen-Einfall - Vor Entdeckung des Fundamentssektors Dient der Einordnung in der Historie Faden bindet sich an die Amtswaffe, nachdem Trench als Direktor ausfällt Das Älteste Haus gilt fortan zum Großteil als gesäubert Das Zischen entkommt durch den Diaprojektor in eine andere Dimension, statt vollständig vernichtet zu werden Jesse Faden
Diaprojektor

item.title: Isolierte Verwahrung der Infizierten
item.description:

Research
Panoptikon
Dylan Faden

item.title: Astralebene
item.description:
Endloses, weißes Void Schwebende, schwarz-gelbliche geometrische Strukturen in sich wandelnden Mustern Eine riesige schwarze Pyramide ist stets sichtbar — Mittel, über das der Vorstand mit Besuchern kommuniziert Erscheinungsbild reagiert auf Kontext (z.B. rot und fließend während Zischen-Besessenheit, grau und pyramidenlos in Anwesenheit „des Ehemaligen") Keine fixen, eigenständig benannten Unterorte bekannt — die Ebene gilt selbst laut Bureau als formlos und ständig wandelnd Zwei dokumentierte, missionsgebundene Erscheinungsformen: „Astralebene (Threshold Kids)" und „Astralebene (Forschung)" — Details dazu liegen noch nicht vor
Der Vorstand
Physischer Kontakt mit einem Object of Power kann unfreiwillig hierher teleportieren, siehe Astralreisen & Thresholds
Direkte Verbindung zum Ältesten Haus über Der Nagel im Fundamentssektor

item.title: Der Zischen-Einfall
item.description:
Das Zischen überrennt das Älteste Haus Lockdown des gesamten Hauses Direktor Zachariah Trench verschwindet in die Astralebene, ebenso Casper Darling - Nach Trenchs Kontakt mit dem Zischen in Slidescape-36 - Vor Fadens Säuberung des Hauses Dient der Einordnung in der Historie Trench wird in Slidescape-36 dem Zischen ausgesetzt und beginnt sich zu verändern Die Resonanz breitet sich über das Haus aus, korrumpiert Personal und Bausubstanz Großteil des Personals wird korrumpiert oder muss evakuiert werden Das Haus geht in Lockdown, Direktorenposten vakant
Zachariah Trench
Casper Darling
Central Executive

item.title: Entdeckung des Fundamentssektors
item.description:
Direktorin Faden erschließt über OoP002 den bis dahin unbekannten Fundamentssektor Untersuchungs- und Forschungsteams werden entsandt, um den Sektor unter Kontrolle des FBC zu bringen - Nach Fadens Säuberung des Hauses - Parallel zu - Isolierte Verwahrung der Infizierten - Vor der aktuellen DEM-Expedition Dient der Einordnung in der Historie Datiert auf 20.05.2019 laut Bureau-Dokument OoP002 zeigt Faden den Weg zum Fundamentssektor Die meisten zugänglichen Bereiche werden erkundet, Proben an die Dimensionale Forschung übergeben Ein letztes Aufräumteam findet ungewöhnliche Spuren, die auf das Zischen hindeuten — Auslöser der aktuellen Expedition
Jesse Faden
Fundamentssektor
Research

item.title: Emily Pope
item.description:
Head of Research des FBC War Forschungsassistentin von Casper Darling, wurde nach dessen Verschwinden während der Zischen-Invasion offiziell seine Nachfolgerin Head of Research Leiterin der Abteilung der Dimensionalen Forschung
Research
Nachfolgerin von Casper Darling
Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Jesse Faden
Führt vertrauliche Gespräche mit Dylan Faden (P6) Die Zischen-Infektion wissenschaftlich verstehen (Arbeitshypothese: geräuschbasierte Übertragung, menschliches Bewusstsein spielt zentrale Rolle) Darlings Forschung fortführen Hat das DEM-Programm reaktiviert, um langfristig mehr Ressourcen für ihre Abteilung zu bekommen
Analysiert P6's Aussagen über Polaris und Hedron-Resonanz für Faden Wie weit ist sie bereit zu gehen, um ihre Hypothesen zu bestätigen?

item.title: Jesse Faden
item.description:
Aktuelle Direktorin des FBC Band nach Trenchs Verschwinden die Amtswaffe und wurde dadurch vom Vorstand als neue Direktorin bestätigt Direktorin des FBC Trägerin der Amtswaffe Begleitet von Polaris
Central Executive
Bruder: Dylan Faden (P6), in Verwahrung
Begleiterin seit Kindheit: Polaris
Vorgänger im Amt: Zachariah Trench
Enge Zusammenarbeit: Emily Pope Das Zischen endgültig besiegen Ihren Bruder Dylan heilen bzw. befreien Aktuell: verfolgt eine Spur des Zischens, das durch den Diaprojektor in eine andere Dimension entkommen ist
Aktuell abwesend auf wichtiger Mission, lässt Simon Arish die Einweisung der DEM-Rekruten übernehmen Was passiert, wenn sie nicht zurückkehrt?

item.title: Polaris
item.description:
Rätselhafte, resonanzbasierte Entität Begleitet Jesse Faden seit dem „Ordinary AWE" in ihrer Kindheit Quelle von Fadens parautilitärischen Fähigkeiten Führte Faden zum Ältesten Haus Keine offizielle — agiert unabhängig, aber laut Faden verbündet mit dem Vorstand gegen das Zischen
Begleitet Jesse Faden seit Kindheit
Verhältnis zu Hedron bewusst ungeklärt: Hedron diente wohl als Gefäß/Kanal für Polaris' Resonanz, beide sind aber wohl nicht dasselbe — siehe Hedron-Resonanz Nach Hedrons Zerstörung wird Faden selbst zum neuen Kanal für Polaris' Resonanz
Dylan Faden misstraut Polaris zutiefst Unbekannt — bewusst nicht aufgelöst Ursprung, wahre Natur und Ziele bleiben Mysterium Nicht auflösen — dient als offener Erzählfaden für das Setting

item.title: Simon Arish
item.description:
Sicherheitschef des FBC Sicherheitschef Militärische Verbindungsperson der Direktorin Security
Direkter Kontakt zu Jesse Faden Übernimmt in ihrer Abwesenheit Einweisung und Leitung Überleben seiner Truppen Physische Sicherheit des Exekutivsektors und der übrigen Sektoren Leitet quasi-offiziell die aktuelle DEM-Expedition, da Faden abwesend ist Wie viel weiß er wirklich über die Hintergründe der Mission?

item.title: Central Executive
item.description:
Verwaltungs- und Führungsebene des FBC Sitzt in der Central Executive (Halle) im Exekutivsektor Verwaltung und Kontrolle des Bureaus aufrechterhalten Ressourcen an die übrigen Abteilungen verteilen Krisenmanagement seit der Zischen-Invasion
Direktorin Jesse Faden an der Spitze (aktuell auf Mission abwesend)
Board Room als zentraler Sitzungsort Höchste Clearance-Stufen im Haus Zugriff auf das Direktorenbüro Letztentscheidung über Sektorzuteilungen und Sonderprojekte wie das DEM-Programm Formal allen anderen Abteilungen übergeordnet
Genehmigt Ressourcenanträge von Research (z.B. für die Abteilung der Dimensionalen Forschung)
Jesse Faden (Direktorin) Fadens Abwesenheit hinterlässt ein Führungsvakuum Wer trifft in ihrer Abwesenheit welche Entscheidungen, und mit welcher Legitimation?
Der Board Room zeigt vierzehn Direktorenporträts in chronologischer Reihenfolge, darunter Zachariah Trench Ein Charakter könnte hier zum ersten Mal begreifen, wer sein Vorgänger im Amt war

item.title: Security
item.description:
Sicherheitsabteilung des FBC Zuständig für physische Sicherheit des Ältesten Hauses Bedrohungen abwehren, physische Sicherheit aller Sektoren gewährleisten Zischen-Vorfälle eindämmen, bis Containment übernehmen kann Sicherheitschef Simon Arish Waffenkammern, Ausbildungseinrichtungen Übernimmt bei Abwesenheit der Direktorin oft faktisch die Einsatzleitung
Unterstützt Containment bei Eindämmungsoperationen
Arbeitet Central Executive direkt zu
Simon Arish (Sicherheitschef) Arish leitet in Fadens Abwesenheit die Einweisung neuer DEM-Rekruten Wie viel Verantwortung ist er bereit, über seine eigentliche Rolle hinaus zu übernehmen?

item.title: Amtswaffe
item.description:
Object of Power, katalogisiert als OOP1-KE Geborgen am 04.08.1964, kurz nach Entdeckung des Ältesten Hauses Wählt selbst ihren Träger — wer sie bindet, wird vom Vorstand als neue Direktorin/neuer Direktor bestätigt Eine von nur zwei Objects of Power, die für Nicht-Direktoren tödlich sind (neben der Hotline)
In dieser Kampagne kein Spielercharakter-Item — nur als Lore-/NPC-Objekt relevant (z.B. bei Zachariah Trench) Sechs bekannte Feuermodi: Grip, Shatter, Spin, Pierce, Charge, Surge eN (variiert je nach Modus) Q5 Nicht spielbar (Director-only) — Berührung/Nutzung durch andere ist laut Kanon lebensgefährlich

Ursprünglich von Zachariah Trench gebunden, um die Dimensionale Forschung vor dem restlichen Bureau zu verbergen -/- (kein Kampfgegenstand) Q4

item.title: Der Kühlschrank
item.description:
Katalogisiert als AI10-KE — trotz Altered-Item-Kürzel zusätzlich in der Objects-of-Power-Kategorie gelistet (uneinheitlich, siehe Objects of Power & Altered Items) Muss ständig beobachtet werden, sonst „weicht er ab" — ein Agent, der den Blickkontakt unterbrach, wurde getötet Verbunden mit einer astralen Entität namens „der Ehemalige" Ein Kinderzeichnung klebt am Kühlschrank und lässt sich nicht entfernen — Hinweis, dass er einst harmloser war -/- (Gefahr durch Unterlassen, kein aktiver Angriff) Q4
Altered Item — siehe Objects of Power & Altered Items

item.title: Diaprojektor
item.description:
Object of Power — projiziert fotografische Dias, die als Türen zu anderen Dimensionen fungieren Laut Bureau-Akte nie von einem Parautilitarier erfolgreich gebunden worden — seine Dimensionseffekte aktivieren sich auch ungebunden von selbst Erste Entdeckung durch die Kinder Jesse und Dylan Faden 1954-2002 in Ordinary, Maine (siehe Ordinary-AWE-Flügel) Auslöser der gesamten Dimensionalen Forschung sowie der Entdeckung von Hedron
Über ihn wurde das Zischen aus dem Ältesten Haus vertrieben — siehe Fadens Säuberung des Hauses -/- (kein Kampfgegenstand) Q5
Objects of Power — siehe Objects of Power & Altered Items
Siehe auch Astralreisen & Thresholds

Lindwurm (Japanese: リントヴルム, Rintovurumu) is an organization and family of enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. They are terrorists aiming to bring down the Empire of Mor Ardain using any means necessary. They seem to be affiliated with the Brionac, who have similar goals.
Their members comprise mostly of Ardainian soldiers, but they also have some Titan weapons, attack dogs, and Drivers. Most of them are found at Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago, although some are found elsewhere during certain quests.

item.title: Der Vorstand
item.description:
Mächtige, paranormale Entitäten aus der Astralebene Kommunizieren über die Hotline Bestätigt neue Direktoren via Bindung an die Amtswaffe Übergeordnete, kaum greifbare Autorität über das FBC Keine — eigenständige Macht aus der Astralebene
Verbündet mit Polaris/der Direktorin gegen das Zischen — aber selbstinteressiert, hält „alle anderen für entbehrlich"
Verbunden mit dem Ältesten Haus über den Nagel im Fundamentssektor Unklar — eigene Agenda, bewusst nicht aufgelöst Die Hotline im Direktorenbüro: nur die Direktorin darf gefahrlos abnehmen Jeder andere erleidet schwere psychische Schäden — ein hervorragendes „bitte nicht anfassen"-Objekt für neugierige Spielercharaktere

item.title: Dylan Faden
item.description:
Jüngerer Bruder von Jesse Faden „Prime Candidate 6" im Prime-Candidate-Programm des FBC (Nachfolgersuche für den Direktorenposten) Nach dem „Ordinary AWE" 2002 gemeinsam mit Jesse als Kind vom FBC aufgenommen In Verwahrung gehalten (P6-Zelle im Panoptikon), vom Zischen korrumpiert Containment (als Verwahrungsobjekt)
Bruder von Jesse Faden, nennt sie „meine liebe Schwester"
Misstrauisch bis feindselig gegenüber Polaris Unklar — äußert sich nur noch kryptisch Wirft Faden vor, von Polaris manipuliert zu werden Führt vertrauliche Gespräche mit Faden über Polaris und Hedron-Resonanz Seine Hinweise sind wahr, aber absichtlich unvollständig oder verdreht formuliert

item.title: The Pit
item.description:
[](https://control.fandom.com/wiki/The_Pit#articleComments)[Sign In to Save](https://auth.fandom.com/register?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fcontrol.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FThe_Pit%3Fcollections%3Dsave&uselang=en&metadata=collections-save-button "Sign In to Save") Edit
Research Sector, Oldest House
Mold-1
The Pit is a location within the Research Sector of the Oldest House. It is the deepest region of the Active Threshold.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 Related missions
4 Collectibles
5 Notes
6 Gallery
The Pit was the originating point of the Mold outbreak within the Oldest House, where the source of the Mold, an entity classified by Raya Underhill as Mold-1, took residence.
The Pit is only accessible via the side mission Old Growth, after Dr. Underhill synthesizes the Mold cure pill for Jesse. Within the Active Threshold is a large pit shrouded in purple haze; at the bottom of this pit is the Active Threshold Sublevel. Another shaft found near the Active Threshold Sublevel Control Point will lead further down, into the Pit; Levitate must be used in order to mitigate fall damage.The pit itself is a large, open arena with four rock outcroppings surrounding the center and a few more outcroppings along the walls. Initially, the ceiling of the arena is covered with a large number of explosive growths, and the area is shrouded with Mold fumes around the central growth from which Mold-1 emerges. After Mold-1 is defeated, a new room will be opened up to the side, in which The Pit Control Point can be found. This Control Point is the only way to exit the Pit.Upon subsequent returns to the area, there will no longer be explosive growths on the ceiling of the arena, and Mold-1's central growth will have disappeared.
Old Growth: Mold-1 must be defeated to cut off the source of the Mold.
Threshold Log 3 - located in a corner near the Control Point, to the right of the floodlight. The entrance area of the Active Threshold is also labelled as "the Pit" upon entering from the elevator shaft. Apart from Mold-1, no other enemies spawn within the Pit.

Synchronicity Lab is a location in the Oldest House's Research Sector connected to Ritual Division. Upon entering the room, you will see different containment cells, and eventually a hallway that leads down to another room. This then leads to the Mirror Testing Lab, where the Victorian Mirror can be found and requires Clearance Level 6.
One mission connected to the Synchronicity Lab is Self-Reflection, in which you have to defeat esseJ.
The Threshold Kids multimedia Keeping Secrets can be unlocked in room 4.
A Mod can be unlocked by synchronizing all Newton's cradles in room 3, in both their mirrored and original versions.
Room 3 shaking when all the Newton's cradles are synchronized is a possible reference to mechanical resonance.

Central Research is a location within the Research Sector of the Oldest House. It is the central hub of the Research Sector, with the Sector Elevator and connections to Luck & Probability, the HRA Lab, the Firebreak and Dr. Darling's Office for example. Central research has very blocky and squared off architecture with large trees standing in the middle.
On one of the walls, there is an office that Jesse can not reach without getting to high ground and either evading into it or firstly shooting the windows of the office, then levitating into it. Inside the office is a normal office layout. At the top of the Central Research, there is a balcony that Jesse can levitate to. The balcony has stairs, taking the stairs down will lead to a sound booth area. Interestingly, activating the sound in the sound booth will make objects near the speakers start to float including Jesse's attire.
The prominent stairways in Central Research were inspired by Japanese architect Kenzō Tange’s work in the Kurashiki City Art Museum in Okayama, Japan.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Central_Research#cite_note-1)

Research Sector

The Ashtray Maze is a paranatural pathway found in the Research Sector of the Oldest House, just one of the many locations that Jesse Faden visits in Control. Its purpose is to prevent anyone without the Director's personal clearance from accessing Dimensional Research and the Hedron Chamber beyond.
1 Summary
2 See also
3 Trivia
4 Gallery
The Ashtray Maze is a labyrinth of shifting corridors created by the Ashtray Object of Power under the binding of Director Trench in order to safeguard Dimensional Research and the Slide Projector. The nature of the maze causes anyone who happens upon it to become hopelessly lost or turned around, and permits only the one bound to the OoP (as well as those they designate) to pass through.
Ahti is able to freely traverse the maze with no more difficulty than he would find in traversing the rest of the Oldest House, and in gifting his cassette player to Jesse, she is able to navigate the maze with a similar freedom. Though never conclusively stated, it is extremely unlikely that Trench granted natural passage through the maze to Ahti, due to his distrust of supernatural entities and his critical need to secure the areas beyond. It is known that there are civilians lost in the maze from prior to the Ashtray's retrieval by the FBC.The Ashtray OoP itself is bound to Director Trench, though it is not made clear what effects his death has on this binding. It is possible that Jesse's initial attempt to traverse the maze returned her to the entrance because of Trench's death or because she had taken over as director. Hiss are encountered in the maze, but they seem to be focused on attacking Jesse rather than traversing the maze itself. Additionally, the maze in several instances prevents the Hiss from being able to reach Jesse — this indicates that the maze perhaps protects those with traversal privileges.
The first traversal by Jesse allows the player to fully experience the maze. Subsequent traversals teleport the player to near the end and back to the entrance. Reentering the original maze (without restarting the game) is only possible through the SHÜM 2 arcade cabinet.
Ashtray and Cigarette (Collectible)
Janitor Complaint
Ashtray Maze (Collectible)
The Ashtray maze was directly inspired by the hotel fire scene in the film Barton Fink by the Coen brothers.

The Active Threshold, also known as the Mold Threshold,1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Active_Threshold#cite_note-1) is a Threshold active in the Oldest House which can be found in the Research Sector.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 See also
4 Gallery
5 References
The Threshold consists of a large sublevel under the Research Sector proper which is now abandoned and coated in plant-like and fungal-like growths, and emerged in the Oldest House in 2019, being a recent threat. This "Mold" takes over all living things within in range of influence, including humans - and the area is populated with various humans who have fallen under its sway and become Mold Hosts.
This threshold is believed to be the source of the Mold, and the area is currently under study by Raya Underhill. Sometime before the Hiss invasion, a Ranger squad under the command of Ranger Captain Ramsay entered the Threshold and even set up a Control Point. However, they all succumbed to the effects of the Mold, though their Control Point remains functional once it is cleansed.
In the midst of the Hiss invasion, Jesse Faden entered the Mold Threshold to stop the threat, eventually discovering and defeating the source of the Mold, a monstrous entity called Mold-1 within an even deeper area of the Threshold known as the Pit.The mold is described as the result of incompatible molecular structures from different dimensions interacting, with the dominant one overriding the inferior one. The mold may therefore simply be a form of matter native to an extremely alien dimension. The mold takes over all living things within its range of influence, including humans.

Federal Bureau of Control
The Research Sector is a sector of the Oldest House. It is the location where the Federal Bureau of Control conducts research into a wide variety of paranatural phenomena under the direction of the Head of Research - most recently Dr. Casper Darling, and educational videos created by him can be found throughout Central Research (as well as other areas of the Oldest House) detailing information about the phenomena the Bureau studies.
1 Description
2 Locations
2.1 Central Research
2.1.1 Cafeteria
2.1.2 Dr. Darling's Office
2.2 Parakinesiology
2.3 Parapsychology

2.3.2 Astral Exhibition
2.3.3 Extrasensory Lab
2.4 Active Threshold
2.4.1 The Pit
2.5 Ritual Division
2.5.1 Luck & Probability
2.5.2 Synchronicity Lab
2.5.3 Protective Studies
2.6 HRA Lab

2.8 Dimensional Research
2.8.1 Slide Projector Research
2.8.2 Projector Room
2.8.3 Hedron Resonance Lab
2.8.4 Hedron Chamber
3 Map
4 Gallery
The main room of the Research Sector is multiple stories high, with a group of enormous trees in the center. Various rooms and divisions within the Research Sector are dedicated to researching different paranatural topics, including parapsychology, parakinesiology, dimensional sciences, and the Astral Plane.
The central hub of the Research Sector, with the Sector Elevator and connections to Dimensional Research, Luck & Probability, Ritual Division, HRA Lab, and the Active Threshold.Located on the lowest level of Central Research.
Dr. Casper Darling's unruly office is located on an uppermost floor of Central Research. Various papers there depict a mysterious hexagonal symbol seen in many places throughout the Oldest House. The Altered Item containment file for Arctic Queen is also located on a desk there.
The Parapsychology Division is a section of the Research Sector that contains a variety of different subdivisions. An elevator connects it to an upper level of Central Research that leads to Luck & Probability.
The Hypnosis Lab contains the X-Ray Light Box Object of Power. The Object possesses the Seize ability, and all nearby enemies are apparently entranced by it. Interacting with the Object sends Jesse to the Astral Plane, where she can bind with the Object and gain the Seize ability.
One section of Parapsychology is dedicated to research on the Astral Plane. This section includes a rough model of the topography of the Astral Plane as well as images and video of entities from within it. Outside of this section is a containment cell for an Astral Spike.
In the basement of the Research Sector is an active Threshold, known as the Mold Threshold. Within the Threshold, a group of unknown, plant-like humanoid enemies will attack Jesse if she approaches.The central area of the Mold Threshold. It is normally accessed with a service elevator, but Jesse must first descend into The Pit and restore power to the elevator to use it.
A large hall off of Central Research that connects to Luck & Probability, the Synchronicity Lab, and Protective Studies. Direct access from Central Research is blocked due the Hiss invasion, but it can still be reached by passing through Luck & Probability.
The Luck & Probability area is where Jesse first meets Helen Marshall. It connects Central Research to the Ritual Division.
Later, after Jesse obtains Clearance Level 5, she can return to Luck & Probability to complete an easter egg that rewards the Golden Suit Outfit and some mods. The easter egg involves several simple interactions: In the office section: Pick the four-leaf clover Activate both Newton's crade desk toys Activate the lucky cat statue Flip the horseshoe until the open side of the "U" is facing upwards Use Launch to pick up the golden fish statue and carry it into the experiment chamber In the experiment chamber: Place the four-leaf clover in the planter Turn on all four desk lamps (they are all turned off when first entering the chamber) Place the golden fish near the roulette table, but outside the red zone Finally, spin the roulette wheel and back out of the red zone surrounding the roulette table before the wheel stops spinning, taking care to stand close to the golden fish If all conditions have been met, when the roulette wheel stops the adjacent television set will display the number 7 and the rewards will be added to Jesse's inventory. If a procedure has been missed, the television will display the number 8 and cause strange things to happen, such as the fire sprinklers go off, stacks of papers in the office section will scatter, and a phone will ring.
An area where experiments are conducted to study the effects of synchronicity. Inside is the Mirror Testing chamber, which contains the Victorian Mirror Altered Item.An area where dangerous paranatural phenomena and Altered Items are studied. It connects to the HRA Lab.The location Dr. Casper Darling's Hedron Resonance Amplifier research and production. A special door to Central Research can be unlocked from inside.
The Ashtray Maze is separated from the rest of the Research Sector by a Firebreak on either side. Created by the Ashtray and Cigarette Object of Power, the Maze is an area of the Oldest House that constantly shifts. Only individuals bound to the Ashtray and Cigarette and those they designate may pass through, all others are redirected back to the start of the Maze.
The Dimensional Research area, on the other side of the Ashtray Maze, is where tests were conducted with the Slide Projector.
The Hedron Chamber within Dimensional Research is where the Hedron is contained. It is protected by a huge Hedron Resonance Amplifier, and is likely the single most secure part of the Oldest House that Jesse is able to access.

The Operations Center is a location within the Investigations Sector of the Oldest House. It is the area that divides the Abandoned Offices along with the rest of the Sealed Firebreak and the Active Investigations area which acts as the central hub.
There are nine monitoring stations on one side of the room, each dedicated to a different location, several of which have been the sites of a known AWE. Ballard, Utah
Bright Falls, Washington Pemberton, New Jersey Lansing, Michigan New York, New York Rocky Mount, Virginia
Ordinary, Maine
Keystone
Sterling, Colorado
While Keystone is the sole location without a state listed, there are several wall maps found in the Abandoned Offices that hint it may be Keystone, Florida.

The Investigations Sector is a sector of the Oldest House.
1 Description
1.1 Closure
1.2 Hiss Invasion
2 Areas
3 Map
4 Hidden Locations
5 Trivia
6 Achievements and trophies
7 Gallery
The Investigations Sector was once the domain of the Federal Bureau of Control's Investigations Department, which conducted investigations of paranatural phenomena (such as Altered World Events and paracriminals), and had oversight authority over all members of the FBC itself, including the Director. The Head of Investigations was William Kirklund.
In 2017, Emil Hartman, who had been apprehended by the FBC and imprisoned in the Investigations Sector after he merged with the Dark Presence, inexplicably escaped containment after the FBC brought Alice Wake in for questioning in relation to the Bright Falls AWE, and rampaged across the sector. Kirklund and several other members of the department escaped to the sector lobby across the Firebreak and sealed off the sector's main area behind them, but dozens of FBC agents and huge volumes of important files were left behind. The trapped agents could be heard begging for the Firebreak doors to be opened until Hartman got to them. Director Zachariah Trench, by then already under the influence of The Hiss and upset with Kirklund's investigations into the Prime Candidate Program and his own erratic behavior, held Kirklund responsible for the incident.
The Investigations Department was left severely diminished, and had to make do with insufficient staff and resources. It was also forced to operate entirely in the cramped sector lobby despite making multiple requests to relocate to new offices, implied to be because Trench was intent on marginalizing Kirklund. Kirklund finally resigned from the FBC in 2019, and Chief Investigator Remy Denis was appointed interim department head.
When the Hiss invasion in October 2019 eventually reached into the Investigations Sector, the Hiss resonance merged with Dark Presence that had already possessed Hartman, twisting his body into a hybrid of the two paranatural forces. Director Jesse Faden ventured into the sector after receiving visions from Alan Wake and unsealed it, unaware of the lurking threat. Frederick Langston remotely helped her navigate the Investigations Sector to hunt Hartman down before he could reach the rest of the Oldest House.

When you exit the elevator room, drop down to ground level and behind you, turn around to observe a picture hanging on the wall. The wall here is destructible; the hidden location is just behind it.
In the Observation Deck, the elevator shaft to the left can be entered by removing all the debris blocking it with Launch. Dropping into the shaft will mark the hidden location as discovered, and a yellow supply crate can be found at the bottom. From the shaft, Emil Hartman will then appear outside and attempt to reach inside. He will then move away, and will not be encountered after entering the Transit Tunnel.
Directly inside the entrance area of the Shifted Offices; look up to see a stairway which can be reached using Levitate and float up to either the stairs or the shifted alcove above it. There is a yellow supply crate in the corner of the alcove. In the Abandoned Offices, the far left office rooms has a breakable wall that Jesse can break which leads into another office room which doorway was blocked by office equipment. Entering will reveal a loot-box. ...
The transport hallway east of the junction in the southwest corner of the Eagle Limited AWE can be accessed by jumping out of a window in the utility corridor above. This area references the Movie Camera boss fight which takes place in The Foundation: A train flatbed can be found along with a floodlight, which can be activated to illuminate the area in blue. There is a radio on the train flatbed which plays the music heard during the fight.

Pneumatics is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 Collectible
4 Gallery
Pneumatics is a section of the Communications Department. It houses the mechanical systems of the mail tube network used by the Federal Bureau of Control in the Oldest House.
During the Hiss invasion, the Floppy Disk Object of Power was corrupted by the Hiss and ended up in Pneumatics, killing several Bureau personnel including L. Samson by launching mail tubes and other objects at them. During the main story mission Unknown Caller, Jesse Faden traverses Pneumatics and cleanses the Floppy Disk, obtaining the Launch ability. Hiss Guards, Hiss Rangers, and Hiss Demolition Experts enter the area right after she does so.
Pneumatics is a large space demarcated by six large machines, with an elevated walkway level leading to the machine which controls the Oldest House's mail tube system. From the entrance, the staircase in front leads down into the main floor space, while the path left leads into a side room that has a single secured unit. To reach the elevated walkway, the platform on the right must be reached by traversing the main floor. A Clearance Level 2-locked room contains a Collectible. The staircase here leads up to the catwalk, which can be used to reach the far north platform, where the Floppy Disk is located during Unknown Caller. During Unknown Caller, the Floppy Disk will periodically launch objects at Jesse while she is in Pneumatics.
Havana Supplement - Inside the southeast Clearance Level 2-locked room.

Executive: Personnel ProtectionTechnicalEXECUTIVE_MAILROOM
The Mail Room is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 Collectibles
4 Gallery
The Mail Room is a section of the Communications Department. It is part of the Bureau's internal mail transportation system. The Mail Room also houses the office of the Head of Communications, through which the Hotline Chamber can be reached. Alberto Tommasi, the most recent Head of Communications, was corrupted in the Hiss invasion and must be fought by Jesse Faden when she enters the Mail Room for the first time.
The Mail Room is also the site of Executive: Personnel Protection, which is a repeatable Bureau Alert. During this mission, friendly Bureau personnel will be fighting against waves of Hiss enemies in the Mail Room.
The Mail Room is a large rectangular space with three levels, entered via the Communications Dept.. The Mail Room Control Point can be found just outside the Mail Room itself. It has three entrances: one on the first floor and two on the second floor. All three doors are locked with Clearance Level 1, and only the door on the first floor can be unlocked from the outside.Around the open middle space of the first floor, the second level acts as an overhang covering the first floor's edges. Eight mail tube columns are interspersed around the edges of the Mail Room, extending all the way up into its ceiling. The edges of the room can be used as cover from the attacks of Hiss-corrupted Tommasi during his boss fight. One Collectible can be found on the first level, on the most northwestern mail tube column.The second level can be accessed via stairs along the north and south walls. The office of the Head of Communications, Alberto Tommasi, can be found on this level, at the very western end of the room. Tommasi's office contains three Collectibles as well as one secured unit hidden behind the central console. From here, the Hotline Chamber can be accessed.
There is a third level of catwalks above the second floor along the north and south walls, only accessible via the Levitate ability. A secured unit can be found on this level.
Tommasi's ID: Inside Tommasi's office, on the console to the right from the entrance.
Butte Summary: Inside Tommasi's office, on the floor near a small cart between the room's entrance and exit.
Tee Time: On the first floor of the Mail Room, on the most northwestern mail tube column.
Tommasi: AWE Report: Inside Tommasi's office, on the main console with the large display board.

The Hotline Chamber is an area in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House.
1 Background

The Hotline Chamber, located within the FBC's Communications Department, houses the Hotline Object of Power, which functions as a direct line of communication with the Board.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Hotline_Chamber#cite_note-1) The Director is the only person allowed to enter the Hotline Chamber and use the Hotline itself; anyone else who tries to use the Hotline will receive fatal psychic trauma from the Object.2(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Hotline_Chamber#cite_note-2) However, Bureau janitors are still allowed to enter the Hotline Chamber for routine cleaning.3(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Hotline_Chamber#cite_note-3)
During the Hiss invasion, Jesse Faden enters the Hotline Chamber to access the Hotline in order to receive clear messages from the apparition of the deceased Zachariah Trench. The walkway to the central chamber is not extended, so Jesse first traverses the Oceanview Motel via a conveniently-placed light switch cord, and upon her return the walkway has appeared.
The Hotline Chamber itself is a large spherical chamber with a small glass enclosure in the middle, containing the Hotline on a table and a small chair. Outside the chamber is a foyer with a security checkpoint, which initially only connects to the Mail Room. After accessing the Hotline during Unknown Caller, a new hallway appears which connects the Hotline Chamber all the way back to the inside of the Director's Office.
Butte Supplement: On the mail tube station in the foyer.
Hotline Security Log: On a filing cabinet at the security checkpoint.

Executive Affairs is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House.
1 Background
2 Layout
2.1 Hidden Location
3 Collectibles
4 Notes
5 Gallery
Executive Affairs is one of the first areas visited by Jesse Faden after she becomes the Director of the Federal Bureau of Control, forced to fight Hiss Guards in order to pass through and gain access to Central Executive.
Executive Affairs also appears in the nightmare that Jesse experiences after Hedron is destroyed by the Hiss, where she is forced to complete repetitive office work as a new low-level Bureau employee until she finally realizes and breaks free of the cycle.
Executive Affairs consists of a set of divided rooms in the west and a more open area in the east. The western and southwestern side of the area holds meeting rooms separated by staff restrooms, with an office in the middle belonging to Mike Hill, who has unfortunately become a Hiss Agent. The eastern half is centered around a large pillar, with a large desk area in the southeast. A Safe Room in the east contains a Collectible and a secured unit.
There are two exits from this location, one leading to the Director's Office in the northwest and to Central Executive in the northeast.
A new room opens up in the south wall, between the meeting room and the desk area, after completing Take Control, although it is also shown on the area map for the entire game. This room is completely empty.
A Hidden Location can be found and accessed in Executive Affairs. The area in question is the top of the large pillar, where another secured unit can be found. The Levitate ability is needed to reach this location. After Levitating up once, maneuver to and momentarily land on one of the floating Hiss Agents; this will allow for a second Levitation, which will be enough to reach the top of the pillar.
Dinner Reservations - On a cabinet near the rows of desks in the southeast corner.
Executive Meeting Minutes - In the meeting room in the far west side of the area.
Marshall: AWE Investigations - Inside the Safe Room.
FBC Reminder: Building Shifts - In a meeting room in the southwest corner.
A desk in the northern part of Executive Affairs contains two nameplates for Daniel Jones and Helen Marshall. Marshall's role is listed here as the "Director's Secretary". Marshall's nameplate comes from the Hiss nightmare at the start of Take Control, in which Marshall is not seen but is apparently Zachariah Trench's secretary; its placement in the standard version of the area is most likely unintentional.

Executive SectorTechnicalEXECUTIVE_DIRECTORS_OFFICE
The Director's Office is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House. It is the office of the Director of the Federal Bureau of Control.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 Collectibles
4 Gallery
4.1 Collectible
5 References
This room in the Executive Sector serves as the office of the FBC's director, who most recently was Zachariah Trench. The Hotline, an Object of Power innately tied to the director, was first discovered in the Director's Office.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Director%27s_Office#cite_note-1) The Service Weapon, another Object of Power associated with the director's role, is also claimed to have been found in the office, but this is known to be untrue.2(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Director%27s_Office#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Director%27s_Office#cite_note-3)
During the Hiss invasion, Trench killed himself in his office with the Service Weapon, with his body being found by Jesse Faden moments later.4(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Director%27s_Office#cite_note-4) Jesse Faden subsequently became the FBC's director via the Service Weapon's ritual and the office was made hers.
The Director's Office is a large, mostly empty room holding the desk of the FBC's director. Two of the walls are lined with shelves holding pictures and other memorabilia related to the former director, Zachariah Trench. The wall behind the desk holds an opening which lights up the room. Initially, there is only entrance to the Director's Office in the hallway between Executive Affairs and Central Executive, but at the end of Unknown Caller, a new tunnel opens up which connects the Director's Office to the Hotline Chamber.
Certain minor changes are made to the Director's Office over the course of Control's main story. The body of Zachariah Trench stays in the office and is removed at the end of Unknown Caller, at which point a Collectible is also added to the room (see below.) At the end of Take Control, the final main story mission, the nameplate on the director's desk is updated to read "Jesse Faden" rather than "Zachariah Trench" along with a number of small aesthetic changes to the room in general.
Trench: Bureau Funding - Found on top of the director's desk after returning from the Hotline Chamber at the end of Unknown Caller.

item.description:

[

Oldest House
Executive Sector
The Dead Letters Archive, or simply Dead Letters, is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House. 1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Dead_Letters#cite_note-approval-1)
1 Background
1.1 Events of Control
2 Layout
2.1 Ground levels
2.2 Upper levels
3 Collectibles
4 Gallery
5 References
Dead Letters, opened during Zachariah Trench's directorship by a petition of Penny Bartwell (who subsequently became the head archivist), is a mail archive maintained by the Federal Bureau of Control for "dead letters" (mail deemed by the United States Post Office as unfit for delivery due to having little to no proper regulation efforts in them, such as return addresses and names). It functions as a database for researchers to investigate paranatural connections or topics which may be present in the letters. Many of the letters in question are often highly bizarre and conspiratorial in nature, with topics ranging from theories about airplanes being "fake" to a man claiming that Theodore Roosevelt and John Adams are helping him fix his lawnmower.
While much of the mail ends up possibly having no actual paranatural connections and are instead most likely just the ravings of crackpots, it can still be used to document the public perception of the abnormal. The archive's letters are sourced from the United States Postal Service, which gives the FBC letters which it marks as undeliverable.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Dead_Letters#cite_note-approval-1) The archive is also the location of a Control Point.
One notable incident in the Dead Letters Archive was the discovery of the Moving Letters Altered Item by Penny Bartwell in 2014. The Letters had, up to then, not been recorded as part of the archive's mail collection.2(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Dead_Letters#cite_note-2)
Like with most locations within the Oldest House, The Hiss invasion in the Fall of 2019 caused Dead Letters to be corrupted by the Hiss. Jesse Faden first traverses Dead Letters during her search for the Hotline Object of Power, during which she cleanses the area after defeating a group of Hiss Guards, including an armored guard.3(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Dead_Letters#cite_note-3)
Dead Letters is a rectangular space with five levels, of which the upper three are only accessible using the Levitate ability.
There are two exits on the ground level of Dead Letters. The southern exit leads to the Cafeteria, while the western exit (closest to the Control Point) leads to the Communications Dept.. There are two walkways along the east and west walls which connect the ground floor exits to each other, but they are only usable after the location is cleansed. Below the ground level is a lowered office space with various smaller rooms split off along the east and west walls, which contain Collectibles or secured units. Also note the poorly lit area underneath the southern stairs, where another Collectible and secured unit are located. The room in the northeastern corner near the Control Point is locked, requiring Clearance Level 2 to access.There are three secured units through the ground levels of Dead Letters: In the dark section under the southern staircase In one of the offices along the west wall On top of the filing cabinets along the north wall; use Levitate or climb up the nearby bookshelf stairs [Section needed]A total of 8 Collectibles can be found on the ground floor of Dead Letters.
Book Club: Penny - Lower level, in the east office below the Control Point.
Dead Presidents - Lower level, in the west office below the Control Point.
Fake Planes - Near Control Point, in the Clearance Level 2-locked room.
Floppy Disk - In a room west of the Control Point.
Machine God - Near southern exit, in southwest corner near the elevator.
Missing Momma - Lower level, on the TV in the east office below the Control Point.
Singing Fish - Lower level, in the southwest corner underneath the stairs.
Trench: Dead Letter Approval - Lower level, in the southeast office.

item.title: Communications Department
item.description:
[](https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#articleComments)[Sign In to Save](https://auth.fandom.com/register?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fcontrol.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FCommunications_Dept.%3Fcollections%3Dsave&uselang=en&metadata=collections-save-button "Sign In to Save") EditCommunications Dept.
[
](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/control6745/images/a/ae/Communications_Dept.png/revision/latest?cb=20220705181032 "Communications Dept")FBC department
Oldest House
Executive Sector
The Communications Dept. is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House. It is the location of the Communications Department, a division of the Federal Bureau of Control which handles interactions with public bodies, most commonly in covering up major paranatural events.
1 Background
2 Layout
2.1 Hidden Locations
2.1.1 Office
2.1.2 External Communications
3 Collectibles
4 Gallery
5 References
The Communications Department is responsible for handling all communications with the public, providing cover stories for Bureau operations, Altered Item incidents, and Altered World Events. It is also partially responsible for detecting paranatural incidents via monitoring public communications.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-jasper-1) Apart from external responses, the Communications Dept. is also responsible for facilitating internal Bureau communications and announcements.2(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-2) The mail infrastructure of the Oldest House is handled entirely in this department, from mail tube system maintenance to the actual sorting and delivery of inter-departmental, incoming, and outgoing messages.
This department appears to be a successor to the Department of Public Knowledge and Diversions, which held the same role in the early years of the Bureau, aiming to offer "sufficient yet vague rationale" in order to support public belief in a stable and certain world. Close attunement with the technological and social growth of the outside world was necessary in order to control the ever-quickening spread of information over time.3(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-3) Whatever the case, by 1978, the Bureau division responsible for public messaging was known as the Communications Department.4(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-4)
Various Collectibles in the Oldest House reveal the department's efforts to conceal the paranatural world. In 1986, the Jasper Post Box Altered Item was contained after the department intercepted phone calls detailing the incident.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-jasper-1) In 2011, the department took to spreading hoax videos and theories on the internet in order to create a public explanation of the Kyiv AWE.5(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-5) In 2017, the department covered up the Havana AWE as an attack on U.S. embassy staff by foreign powers using sonic weaponry.6(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-7) Most recently, the Willow AWE in 2019 was passed off as an attack by polar bears forced to migrate due to global warming, with Head of Communications Alberto Tommasi praising the response for using contemporary concerns that would help sell the story to the public.8(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Communications_Dept.#cite_note-8)
Alberto Tommasi, the Bureau's most recent Head of Communications, did not survive the Hiss invasion. He was corrupted and became a Hiss Elevated, killing many surviving agents in the Mail Room and using his access to the Bureau's public announcement system to broadcast the Hiss incantation. Meanwhile, the Floppy Disk Object of Power was also corrupted and ran rampant in Pneumatics, killing another number of survivors.
The Communications Department takes up a large portion of the Executive Sector, occupying the entire upper-left quadrant of the sector. Pneumatics, the Mail Room, and the Hotline Chamber are all part of the Communications Department.
This location is traversed during the main story mission Unknown Caller. From the entrance to the Communications Dept. in Dead Letters, a staircase will lead up to a dead end with a single secured unit. The restrooms on the ground floor are empty. Taking the long hallway down will lead to Pneumatics, as well as a Safe Room with a Collectible at the end of the hallway. During Unknown Caller, the path forwards will be blocked by a Hiss Barrier until the Floppy Disk is cleansed.The next hallway is lined by two large cages filled with letters; these are the Inbound Mail and Outbound Mail rooms, though they are not labelled in game. Each of these cages holds a secured unit, and the eastern cage also contains a Collectible.
At the end of this hallway is a large section of offices and desks outside the Mail Room, spanning three floors. A Clearance Level 1 keycard can be collected near dead Bureau personnel on the first and second floors, necessary for unlocking the Mail Room during Unknown Caller. The Mail Room Control Point can be found on the first floor just outside the Mail Room; this is the only Control Point inside the Comms Dept.
The staircase to the second floor near the Control Point contains a Safe Room with a secured unit and a radio which plays the song "Salmon Soup" by Socks & Ballerinas. Objects of note on the second floor are a Collectible and a whiteboard with text not found anywhere else in the Oldest House. (There is one such unique whiteboard in each of the four base game sectors, though they do not have any purpose other than environmental detail.)The third floor, accessible via stairs on the northern end of the second floor, leads to two unmarked locations, both of which contain Hidden Locations.
This office, consisting of two sections, is found behind a "locked" door which does not require any Clearance Level to unlock. One Collectible can be found on the central cabinet in the outer section. The inner section is covered with Mold and cannot be safely traversed until the side mission Old Growth is completed. One secured unit can be found at the very end of this section. To reach the Hidden Location, simply travel all the way into the Mold-filled section.
Notably, all desks inside this office have nameplates. The names on the desks are real-life Remedy Entertainment employees who worked on Control.
External Communications is a large square room with many Black Rock-lined computer cubicles; this is the only place in the entire Oldest House which has internet access. A Collectible can be found here on a copier machine along the west wall. Entering this room causes Hiss enemies to spawn, up to and including the unique Hiss Ranger miniboss Ranger First Class Coleman. The room can be exited at any time, but note that the enemies can follow Jesse outside of the room.
To reach the Hidden Location, the Levitate ability is required. The Hidden Location is above the room itself, on the pipes and scaffolding just below the ceiling of the room. One secured unit can be up in this area.
Data Breach - Inside External Communications (on the third floor outside the Mail Room.)
Book Club: Samson - In the Safe Room outside of Pneumatics.
Marshall: Lockdown Distinctions - In the Mold-filled office on the third floor outside the Mail Room.
Tommasi: Willow AWE Outcome - In the eastern letter cage, under the word "Dept." on the sector map.
America Overnight Ep. 359 - On the second floor of the offices outside the Mail Room.

item.title: Central Executive
item.description:
[](https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Central_Executive#articleComments)[Sign In to Save](https://auth.fandom.com/register?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fcontrol.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FCentral_Executive%3Fcollections%3Dsave&uselang=en&metadata=collections-save-button "Sign In to Save") EditCentral Executive
[
](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/control6745/images/2/27/Central_Executive_-_Mission_1.png/revision/latest?cb=20220417223757 "Central Executive - Mission 1")Sector hub
Oldest House
Executive SectorTechnicalEXECUTIVE_BASE
Central Executive is a location within the Executive Sector of the Oldest House. It is the main hub of the Executive Sector and also functions as the primary mission hub location in Control. Jesse Faden's abilities and weapons cannot be used while in Central Executive.
Central Executive is the location of the first available Control Point which is also the only Control Point that allows Jesse to change her outfits.
1 Background
1.1 Events of Control
2 Layout
2.1 Ground level
2.2 Second floor
3 Collectibles
4 Gallery
5 References
Central Executive is the heart of the Bureau's administrative affairs. Many of the Bureau's top personnel, including the Head of Research, the Head of Communications, and the Vice Chief of Staff all hold office spaces in Central Executive. Under the orders of Head of Security Lin Salvador, Central Executive also houses the containment enclosure of the Songmaster Jukebox Object of Power. The area's high traffic and location would prevent misuse of the object without reducing its accessibility.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Central_Executive#cite_note-1)
During the Hiss invasion, Central Executive was corrupted and rendered unstable by the Hiss. A small number of Bureau personnel wearing HRAs, including Emily Pope, survived inside a Safe Room.
Central Executive is the first location in the Oldest House to be reclaimed from the Hiss by Jesse Faden, who cleanses its Control Point after defeating the Hiss-corrupted Ranger Second Class Polaski. Because of this, the sector hub becomes the main center of operations for the Bureau's response against the Hiss. As the situation advances, the Bureau's internal security and Rangers direct refugees towards Central Executive,2(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Central_Executive#cite_note-2) while surviving researchers under the lead of Emily Pope put their focus on understanding the Hiss — and how to fight it.
Later into the Hiss invasion, Central Executive also houses Dylan Faden, who has been corrupted by the Hiss but retains his intelligence, or at least some part of it.
[
](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/control6745/images/c/c6/Central_Executive_map_marked.png/revision/latest?cb=20220331015800)Map of Central Executive (second floor rooms given arbitrary labels)
Central Executive is a large cubic room with two floors organized around the central Control Point. See the Collectibles section below for detailed information on the Collectibles in Central Executive.
The ground floor is initially a large empty space, but it will become more and more furnished, and populated by more and more Bureau personnel, as the main story progresses. Helen Marshall will briefly appear here at the end of the main story mission Threshold, while Simon Arish will relocate here and take Marshall's place upon starting the main story mission The Face of the Enemy. The Control Point for Central Executive is also here, directly underneath the large inverted pyramid and flanked by several short pillars.
From the ground floor, the Sector Elevator can be accessed via the hallway in the west to access other Sectors. A Safe Room is located in the northeast corner, with a single Collectible inside. A security checkpoint in the southwest corner leads to the containment cell of the Songmaster Jukebox, which is locked until starting the mission Put a Record On. There is also a Clearance Level 3-locked security room which contains a Collectible, a standard secured unit, and a radio which plays "Constrain" by Byproduct.
The entrance to the Board Room, where Emily Pope stays for the entire main story after the first mission, is on the east wall. A door in the north leads to the Accounting Department and the Cafeteria. A Clearance Level 1-locked security room can be found in the small stairwell just outside the door, with a standard secured unit inside.
The second floor, which encircles the ground level, contains various separate office rooms and two exits. The west hallway leads to just outside the Director's Office, while the south hallway leads to Executive Affairs.For explanation purposes, the second floor rooms will be arbitrarily labelled as shown in the map above.16 total Collectibles can be found in Central Executive.
Prohibited Items Reminder - Found at room C (only if not collected during the introduction).
R4 Reports Reminder - Found inside room A (only if not collected during the introduction).
Security Order - Found inside room B (only if not collected during the introduction).
Shifted Bathroom Complaint - Found inside room D.
Sticky Note Complaint - Found inside room K, the Clearance Level 4-locked room.
Visitor Evaluations - Found inside room H.
Salvador: Security Order - Found on the first floor, near the hallway to the Sector Elevator, after the main story mission Threshold.
America Overnight Results - Found inside the Clearance Level 3-locked security room on the first floor near the Jukebox enclosure.
Bureau Expenditures - Found inside room F (only if not collected during the introduction).
Collective Unconscious - Found on Darling's desk in room J at the end of the main story mission Unknown Caller.
Control Points - Found inside the first floor Safe Room.
Parautility - Found inside room G.
Pope's Promotion - Found on Pope's desk in room J after the main story mission Threshold.
Technological Restrictions - Found inside room B.
Television Proposal - Found on the first floor, near Simon Arish's table after starting the main story mission The Face of the Enemy.
Urban Legends - Found inside room H.

Oldest House
Executive SectorTechnicalEXECUTIVE_EXECUTIVE_CAFETERIA
The cafeteria is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 Collectibles
4 Gallery
5 References
Managed by the Federal Bureau of Control's Department of Unhuman Affairs,1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Cafeteria#cite_note-1) this staff cafeteria serves the employees of the Executive Sector.
The cafeteria is a large, open cubic space with interspersed displays of vegetation. A balcony along the south and east walls hides the line kitchen along the south and an alcove with a Mold-infested Safe Room in the east, while a seating section in the north is covered by a an overhang of plants. Two doorways in the west and north respectively lead to the Communications Dept. and Dead Letters, but only the latter can be used. A staircase in the southwest ostensibly leads to Central Executive, but the doorway is also blocked off. On the ground floor to either side of the staircase are the women's and men's restrooms.
Central Executive is still accessible by climbing the stairs to the balcony and heading through the Accounting Department (in the reverse of how this area is first accessed during Unknown Caller.) The Nostalgia Department, permanently subject to deep Hiss corruption, cannot be entered, and approaching it will cause Jesse to lose health. This area around the balcony is surrounded by many deceased Bureau personnel, Rangers and regular agents alike.
There are three standard resource crates around the cafeteria. One is in the men's restroom, one is in the Safe Room, and one is on the ledge filled with plants along the north wall (to reach it, either Levitate or jump up from the staircase railing.)
Havana Summary: On a chair just outside the Safe Room.
Unstable Area Notice: Inside the women's restroom in the southwest corner.

Oldest House
Executive SectorTechnicalEXECUTIVE_BOARDROOM
The Board Room is a location in the Executive Sector of the Oldest House. It is a distinct subsection of Central Executive.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 Collectibles
4 Trivia
5 Gallery
5.1 Director portraits
The Board Room is an executive meeting room for the Federal Bureau of Control's administrators. During the events of Control, the Board Room is where Emily Pope stays for the entire main story after the first mission, becoming her main office for research into the Hiss.
The Board Room is a long, rectangular room constructed around a central conference table. The far eastern wall is lined with fourteen portraits, including that of Zachariah Trench and the two FBC Directors immediately preceding him. The chronological order seems to be from left to right, where new rows are placed above the older rows. A standard secured unit is also found against the east wall.
As the main story of Control advances, more and more items and supplies will be added to the Board Room, and a series of collectibles will become available. An unnamed Bureau researcher will also be present, assisting Pope.These are listed in sequential order based on the earliest they can be obtained.
Initial Impressions - On the conference table at the end of Unknown Caller.
Linguistic Ability - On the conference table at the end of Old Boys' Club.
Speech Analysis - On the conference table at the end of My Brother's Keeper.
Timeline of Events - On a crate against the wall at the end of My Brother's Keeper.
Variance in Alterations - On the conference table after completing Take Control.
The Board room was heavily influenced by the war room in Stanley Kubrick's 1964 film Dr. Strangelove. Several of the Director portraits are Remedy staff - among them Stuart Macdonald (World Design Director), Paul Ehreth (Lead Designer), and Leonardo Calamati (Principal Concept Artist).

item.description:

Executive SectorTechnicalEXECUTIVE_ACCOUNTING_DEPARTMENT EXECUTIVE_ACCOUNTING_LOBBY_CAFETERIA_JUNCTION
The Accounting Department is an unmarked location within the Executive Sector of the Oldest House, located between the Cafeteria and Central Executive. This is the site of the Accounting Department, a subdivision of the Federal Bureau of Control which manages its financials.
1 Background
2 Layout
3 Notes
4 Gallery
5 References
As a federal agency, the Bureau's primary funding source is the United States federal government. The Accounting Department's main responsibility is to track and compile the Bureau's expenses in order to manage its budget and make suitable budget requests to the government. As part of this process, the department collects expense reports from all of the Bureau's employees and operatives and also releases quarterly fiscal reports.1(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Accounting_Department#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Accounting_Department#cite_note-2) The department also reimburses employees for job-related expenses, although the Oldest House's mail tube system occasionally hinders this system.3(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Accounting_Department#cite_note-3)
The Accounting Department is a single large office room above the Cafeteria. Because the other doorway from Central Executive to the Cafeteria is blocked, the only way to reach the Cafeteria is to pass through this room. The bodies of various Bureau personnel are strewn about inside this room and outside, near the Nostalgia Department. When initially in this location during Unknown Caller, several Hiss Guards are patrolling the Cafeteria balcony outside. On later visits, other Hiss enemies may spawn.
This location contains one loot crate and one collectible (Travel Costs), both of which are found in the large square part of the room.
This area is not specifically labelled as the Accounting Department in-game. The game's files reference a location called the "Accounting Lobby Cafeteria Junction",4(https://control.fandom.com/wiki/Accounting_Department#cite_note-4) indicating that the Accounting Department is near the Cafeteria, and the only location which fits this description is the one listed above.
